meta.source: Luminari WA Registry v1.0 — Northwest Hope Foundation

flags.title: WA Just Cause Eviction Protection
flags.message: Washington requires just cause for eviction under RCW 59.18.650. Landlords must provide specific legal grounds.
action_items: Verify landlord has stated just cause
Check if 14-day or 60-day notice applies
Review local eviction moratorium status

flags.title: WA Basic Food Expanded Eligibility
flags.message: Washington's Basic Food program uses broad-based categorical eligibility with 200% FPL gross income limit. No asset test for most households.
action_items: Check if household qualifies under BBCE
Verify no asset test applies
Note WA uses WashingtonConnection.org for applications

flags.title: WA Apple Health (Medicaid) Expansion
flags.message: Washington expanded Medicaid (Apple Health) to 138% FPL for adults. Covers comprehensive benefits including behavioral health.
action_items: Check Apple Health eligibility
Note behavioral health coverage
Verify managed care plan assignment

flags.title: WA Paid Family & Medical Leave
flags.message: Washington has mandatory Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML) — up to 12 weeks paid leave at 90% of wages up to cap.
action_items: Check PFML eligibility (820 hours worked)
Verify employer compliance with premium payments
Note 12-week duration with possible 16-week combined

flags.title: WA Indian Child Welfare Act (WICWA) Enhanced Protections
flags.message: Washington's WICWA (RCW 13.38) provides protections beyond federal ICWA, including broader definitions of Indian child and active efforts requirements.
action_items: Apply WICWA standards (broader than federal ICWA)
Contact tribe and WICWA liaison
Ensure active efforts documented per RCW 13.38.040

flags.title: WA Utility Shutoff Protections
flags.message: Washington prohibits utility disconnection November 15 – March 15 for low-income households. Medical emergency protections available year-round.
action_items: Check winter moratorium status (Nov 15 – Mar 15)
Verify low-income qualification
Check medical emergency certification

flags.title: WA Elder Abuse Mandatory Reporting
flags.message: Washington has mandatory reporting for elder abuse. Reports must be made to DSHS Adult Protective Services within 48 hours.
action_items: File APS report within 48 hours
Contact local law enforcement if immediate danger
Document all observations

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Washington 72-Hour Hold (ITA)
flags.message: WA involuntary psychiatric hold law: Washington 72-Hour Hold (ITA). Statutory authority: RCW § 71.05.150. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others or gravely disabled. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Verify physician certification was completed
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in WA retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Document any communication restrictions imposed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in WA: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Confirm continuous monitoring was documented
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Washington Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Washington Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
